intent:
"yes approbe and begin the implementation" started the bstack build slice by slice, strictly one at a time ("keep it sequential"). Later: "i'm only not concerned about security hardening, threat-model concerns. Style and simplification and following proper design principles are still important." - build the full app fast, but review the core properly so slices and phases do not leave bugs.

The plans of record are in the repo: `docs/design.md` (requirements and decisions, including R24: licensing is out of scope) and `docs/implementation-plan.md` (tasks, task evidence contract). knowttl/bstack is public, has no GitHub Actions or workflows and no release automation, and ships through the no-mistakes pipeline with automatic merge of green work. Landed: Phase 0, Phase 1, T2.1-T2.6 and T2.7 part 1 (https://github.com/knowttl/bstack/pull/27: check plans, `run-checks` and prior protection, with the simplified contract - inputs fingerprinted once before and once after a run, blocked on any change).

This piece is slice C15b, the rest of task T2.7 "Build verification capture and live probes": the live probe pair. Done evidence: same endpoint/command/environment before and after, local stand-in mismatch, specific side-effect approval refusal.
amendments: C15b completes T2.7 with schema-defined live probe capture, ordered matching pairs, per-call side-effect approval and current-input freshness.
Required installs, package check, full suite and registered T2.7 suite executed against the committed implementation revision.

cases.procedure: bug fix requires normally failing reproduction before and passing reproduction after; a protected refactor passes only after compatibility runs against changed state
ts-shop passing units cannot hide the failed checkout journey
an uncovered user flow remains unverified despite passing units; cancelled required check stays unverified even with other passing checks
ts-shop live stand-in disagrees with the passing mock so its probe pair is not ready; ts-shop passing units cannot hide the failed checkout journey

failed/skipped/unavailable/timed out/failed version required check cannot pass; changed declared inputs block the capture; a later input change blocks all executed checks; unavailable final snapshots retain completed command evidence; invalid scratch setup runs no commands
matching live calls capture literal arguments and pass across changed product inputs without target writes; comparison rejects changed endpoint, command and environment
missing executable retains its reason and cannot verify the pair; comparison rejects a missing before or after probe
side-effect approval is refused before either version or live command and binds only the specific call; a child argument cannot approve a side-effecting call

limitations: 100 targeted tests and 767 full-suite tests passed on Linux Node 24. Real Windows/macOS execution remains captain checklist evidence. No hosted CI ran.

Case mappings establish command-interface controls, not complete fresh-agent acceptance. Local scratch capture trusts declared scopes, endpoint identity, environment keys and the selected assertion command.
Boundary fingerprints do not detect transient input changes restored before completion. Later evidence tasks collect check and probe results into a unified assessment.
